claim: Access to Calanque de Sugiton/Pierres Tombees requires a free advance booking on 20-21 June, every day from 27 June to 30 August, and on 5-6 and 12-13 September 2026, bookable from 9am three days before and closing 6pm the day before, up to 5 people per reservation.
quote: 20-21 June, everyday from 27 June to 30 August, on 5-6 September and on 12-13 September 2026... Reservations are free and open to everyone... Reservations can be made from 9.00 a.m., 3 days prior to your visit... Reservations close at 6.00 p.m. on the day prior to your visit

claim: The Sugiton reservation system caps daily entries at 400 people to combat erosion from peaks of up to 2,500 visitors a day; entry requires a QR code on your phone.
quote: limits daily entries to exactly 400 people... peaks of up to 2,500 visitors a day... Without a QR code on your phone, you cannot enter these restricted areas

claim: Public transport to the Calanques: from Place Castellane or Prado take bus B1 or 21J to the Luminy stop for Sugiton/Morgiou, and bus 23 toward Beauvallon serves Sormiou; from Luminy the hike to a calanque takes about 45 minutes each way.
quote: From Place Castellane or the Prado roundabout, take bus B1 or 21 J to the 'Luminy PN des Calanques' stop... around 45 minutes each way

claim: Roads to Sormiou, Morgiou and Callelongue close to motorized traffic 7am-7pm on Fridays, weekends and public holidays across spring 2026, with closures extendable to 10pm on red-level fire-risk days, and summer weekend/holiday closures from 18 June.
quote: roads to Sormiou, Morgiou, and Callelongue are closed to motorized traffic from 7h to 19h on: Fridays, weekends and public holidays... extended until 22:00 on red-level forest fire risk days

claim: Sugiton is a moderate hike on polished limestone from Luminy with two small swim beaches; En-Vau is the park's most dramatic inlet with a steep rugged descent and no road access reached via Cassis/Port-Pin; the best hiking season is October-May because of June-September fire restrictions and hikers should carry 2 liters of water.
quote: Calanque de Sugiton... Difficulty: Moderate... Calanque d'En-Vau... Difficulty: Rugged, steep descent... no road access... Best Season: October-May (fire restrictions June-September)... Water: 2 liters per person minimum

claim: Icard Maritime boat tours from the Vieux-Port include a 3h15 'Complete Calanques' tour (Sormiou, Morgiou, Sugiton, En Vau, Port-Pin, Port-Miou) at 33 euros and a 2h30 'Essential Calanques' tour at 27 euros, plus a summer-only 3h30 sea-swimming tour at 40 euros.
quote: The Complete Calanques - Duration: 3h15... Sormiou, Morgiou, Sugiton, En Vau, Port-Pin, and Port-Miou... The Complete Calanques: 33; The Essential Calanques: 27... Calanques & Sea Swimming: 40

claim: Two main operators run Calanques boat tours from the corner of Quai des Belges/Quai du Port on the Vieux-Port: Croisieres Marseille Calanques and Icard Maritime, both visiting Sormiou, Morgiou, Sugiton, Devenson, En Vau, Port-Pin and Port-Miou.
quote: Croisieres Marseille Calanques and Icard maritime... Sormiou, Morgiou, Sugiton, Devenson, En Vau, Port-Pin and Port-Miou... corner of Quai des Belges and Quai du Port, Vieux-Port

claim: Plage des Catalans is the closest sandy beach to the Old Port (about a 15-minute walk) with free showers and toilets and lifeguards June-September, while the Prado beaches form a free 3.5km succession of beaches (Roucas Blanc, Prado Nord/Sud, Borely) open year-round.
quote: Plage des Catalans is just a 15-minute walk from the Old Port... free public showers and restrooms... Prado Beaches... freely accessible beaches (Roucas Blanc, Prado Nord, Prado Sud, Plage de Borely...) stretching for 3.5km... free for everyone throughout the year
